subject: Unexpected client-side rejections during evening peak — quota guardrail review
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@brightside.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops+dev@brightside.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Spike of 429s after 5PM PST — immediate help needed

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a spike in 429s and client-side timeouts around 5:05pm PST during our evening user ramp. The app is getting token-denied and request-rejected errors — grid indicates the failures are clustered to short bursts (10–30s) rather than a steady increase. Attached is a CSV with example responses and timestamps.

This is impacting our core booking flow (users can’t submit). Can you confirm whether this is an intentional quota enforcement or a misconfiguration? We’re in the middle of a promo window and need a mitigation plan ASAP.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
CTO, Brightside Health

Hi Maya — thank you for the quick heads-up and the CSV. I’m escalating to our on-call SRE and account team.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi (SRE) is looking at the request logs and quota windows now.
- Neha (Customer Reliability) will coordinate with your ops team for a short-term throughput lift if needed.
- I’ll pull the profile for your tenant’s burst window and guardrails.

From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: maya@brightside.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:46:55 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s after 5PM PST — immediate help needed

Quick findings from the runtime side:
- I see request bursts from Brightside that exceed the configured burst_window for their quota bucket (40 requests in 10s, configured window = 8s).
- The quota guardrail (per-tenant QPS + burst smoothing) is rejecting requests once the rolling-window token bucket is depleted.
- There’s also a secondary pacing rule that activates below 50% remaining tokens and enforces a more aggressive backoff. That was tripped around 17:05.

This looks like a policy misalignment — their traffic profile has short high-intensity spikes (promo traffic). The burst_window on their plan is too small relative to their real-world bursts.

Immediate mitigations I can apply (low risk, quick):
1) Temporarily increase the burst_window for tenant BS-2026-Q4-77 from 8s -> 20s and bump token ceiling by +35% for the next 2 hours.
2) Add a short-lived fallback model route to a lower-cost compatible variant to absorb overflow if rate remains high.

I’ll need approval from Product/Policy to make the burst_window change in prod — pinging Neha and Laura.

-Rishi
Customer Reliability / On-call SRE
From: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 18:02:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s after 5PM PST — immediate help needed

Thanks Rishi, this matches what I’m seeing in the tenant policy dashboard. Laura — we should authorize a temporary burst_window expansion and token ceiling bump while we root cause. Brightside is in a time-sensitive promotion and the impact is customer revenue.

Proposed short-term action (approved by me for immediate ops):
- Apply change: burst_window -> 20s, token_ceiling -> +35% for 2 hours (auto-revert).
- Queue a follow-up policy review to adjust the plan profile for promo windows.

Maya — can your team confirm the expected peak QPS and whether the app will enforce client-side retries with jitter? If not, we’ll coordinate a recommended retry pattern to smooth spikes.

Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Singh <maya@brightside.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops+dev@brightside.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 18:18:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s after 5PM PST — immediate help needed

Thanks — we just confirmed with our ops lead. Peak bursts were hitting ~220 QPS for ~20–30s windows. Our client retry strategy is basic (linear backoff) and wasn’t sufficient during the promo burst. We’ll push a hotfix to add jittered exponential backoff in the next deploy (ETA ~2 hours).

Attaching request traces from our side for correlation. Please proceed with the temporary increase; we’re ready to accept the lower-cost fallback route while we patch.

Maya
---
Attachments: brightside-req-trace-20261220.tar.gz
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@brightside.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s after 5PM PST — temporary change applied + follow-ups

Team — I’ve approved and applied the temporary policy changes described below (burst_window=20s; token_ceiling=+35%) with an auto-revert at 20:30 PST. We also enabled a fallback route to the compatible-moderate model to absorb excess traffic.

Action items and owners:
- Rishi: monitor error rate and confirm the 429s drop to <1% within next 30 minutes (ON IT).
- Neha: coordinate a post-incident policy adjustment for the account (create policy PR + run sim tests).
- Jasmine: confirm with Maya once their client fix is deployed and confirm whether they want us to keep an elevated promo profile for future scheduled windows.

We should treat this as an operations+policy gap: bursts were allowed by SLA assumptions for most customers, but this customer's traffic pattern requires a larger burst window or scheduled promo profiles.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
